scope: A fifth common Client reads the same single-chest static outline in both creative and survival using the shared target_block API; explicit received mode and native state properties, original native inset and North face, separately audited storage shapes/clips, unchanged native Pos/Rotation. Common creative operations/live-mode rejection; read-only preview/static-outline targeting; finite dry walk/jump with predicted released-rest endpoint; a fresh connection explicitly starts/finishes empty-hand stone mining and receives exact-target air. A third fresh connection places default dirt and receives exact-target dirt and one-material consumption; modern additionally receives a fresh processing ACK. A fourth fresh connection exchanges occupied main/hotbar stacks in survival and then a main stack with an empty hotbar in creative, with two fresh destinations. A fifth fresh connection opens a regular single chest through the existing creative interaction, receives complete contents/cursor/constructor-verified player layout, and receives a fresh same-opening slot update after an independent native change from stone 3 to 7. On that same opening, survival exchanges the received storage stack with an empty hotbar, then creative exchanges it back, with two exact fresh destination receipts and independent native chest/player contents. The common creative handle then closes that original opening once, retains honest dispatch/no synthetic close acknowledgement, and refuses re-close/click. After an external chest change to stone 11, the consumer receives a distinct fresh reopening through the existing creative use-on-block fixture, then closes it once in survival and retains close history after disconnect. On the same Client, a survival default player swap moves dirt 2 from main inventory to the empty hotbar after that no-echo close, with explicit SubmittedClose UI basis and actual player-screen-zero revision on modern; creative swaps it back through the same API. Both require exact fresh destinations and retain actual received window/cursor/revision provenance without synthetic zero/player values. Not tools/general mining, arbitrary placement, general container click/open contracts, nonempty/unknown-cursor close or general player-screen UI/crafting interactions, non-default modern item data/crafting, observer continuation or common recovery parity.
result_authority: Storage targeting reads native setup pose and actual Client geometry; independent RCON verifies unchanged Pos/Rotation. Shape/face/point is checked separately against original native method fixtures, not a server hit acknowledgement, menu ownership or linked opening result. Vanilla server RCON for creative outcomes, unchanged preview/targeting/mining/placement position, target stone/air/dirt and exact dirt inventory count, occupied/empty player inventory exchange contents, survival chest extraction and creative return (exact Items and player Inventory before/after), unchanged chest-operation position, and actual movement samples/endpoint. Target face/point math separately checked against native JAR methods. Client target receipts/frames and Predicted status are not independent server authority or mutation continuation. Close validation records real complete writes and actual distinct reopening; RCON verifies independently changed chest/player contents and position but supplies no menu-state assertion. Sending close does not establish a received close acknowledgement. Post-close player exchanges are checked independently against native player Inventory/chest Items/unchanged position; explicit SubmittedClose in common capture is not a received active-window or revision claim.

failed_mining_stage_trials.reason: Driver sent mining_ready notification as command; stopped before START; corrected stage notification handling.
Read-only preview correctly refused unresolved creative inventory write; fixture now waits for real inventory update from clear before survival preview.

RCON timed out at prior-source disconnect before mining. JVM shutdown dump showed filesystem write wait; forced exit -9, failed. Disposable runtimes moved to /dev/shm to isolate disk I/O, without changing gameplay/receipt guards.

Fast tmpfs fixture reached target query before local grounded geometry settled after teleport; rejected before START, clean exit 0. Consumer now waits using the read-only target query before mutation.

legacy_raw_inventory_primary_check.verification: Local javap of original official 1.16.1 JAR: sender passes window -2 with Inventory.getItem raw index; InventoryMenu constructor appends crafting 0..4, armor raw 39..36, main 9..35, hotbar 0..8 and offhand 40. Original test observations only; no JAR, mappings or bytecode copied into the package.

native_methods_audited: ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleContainerClick (click occurs before stack comparison; matching return suppresses slot updates using ignoreSlotUpdateHack; mismatched return sends negative comparison response plus actual full contents)
legacy_inventory_protocol_oracle.common_contract: One SWAP only. Encode a received nonempty predecessor as retained comparison stack to request native resync. Receive two actual exact destinations and matching comparison response; false comparison does not imply rollback. Existing mandatory protocol response is sent, not a second SWAP. No received slots are synthesized from prediction.
legacy_inventory_protocol_oracle.distribution: Original test observations and source only; no game JAR, mappings or bytecode copied into package.

failed_inventory_stage_trials.reason: Fixture used invalid slot.inventory.0/slot.hotbar.0 command names; official SlotArgument confirmed inventory.0/hotbar.0. Failed before SWAP submission, clean exit 0. Corrected fixture also independently verifies initial inventory.

Correct native empty SWAP return did not provide fresh destination updates before the bounded wait. Official native handler audit explains that matching comparisons suppress slot sends as it assumes client prediction. Common legacy now explicitly requests native resync with a received nonempty comparison stack; no replay/predicted receipt fallback, clean exit 0.

native_menu_layout_oracle.scope: Pinned original official server menu registry and 9 actual storage constructors per version. Total slots and per-Slot identity/reference/raw Inventory mappings, not inferred from packet length. Other menu constructors remain unaudited.

failed_container_stage_trials.reason: Client actually received opening, full contents, changed contents and disconnected. Driver omitted container_disconnect/container_disconnected notification alias and incorrectly failed after the completed consumer. Added exact alias, without changing receipt/gameplay guards; clean JVM exit 0.

native_container_close_oracle.scope: Original unmodified official native packet decode/encode. Legacy two byte IDs plus native protocol packet ID 0x0a; modern three IDs including multi-byte VarInt plus native packet type serverbound/minecraft:container_close. No server/world. Modern ID registration is additionally exercised by the live native scenario; this oracle does not assert RCON menu-state or a received close acknowledgement.

failed_player_screen_stage_trials.reason: Probe asserted unchanged entire observed slot after a complete close write and independent RCON change. Actual delayed receipts are not forbidden by write completion, and RCON handling is not ordered by that write. It failed on legacy before the new post-close player-swap stage. Whether the value or its ordinal changed was not captured. Corrected the fixture to retain actual received history, verify submitted-close UI/re-click refusal, then independently verify actual default player exchanges; no gameplay/receipt guard weakened.

storage_targeting_native_oracle.scope: Original unmodified official 1.16.1/1.21.11 JARs. Seven state-only storage blocks; complete properties, outline/auxiliary; both directions, inset/edge/inside/diagonal and far world coordinates. Animated/world-dependent shapes and native open semantics are not inferred from static targeting.
